courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: The Interplay of Music and Physics
courses.description: How sound is produced in instruments, and how those sounds are used in music making. Wave motion, resonance, sound perception, scales, harmony, and music theory. Collaborative laboratory exercises to investigate the acoustics of string, woodwind, and brass instruments as well as study of the physics of keyboard and percussion instruments. Students will make instruments from found objects and perform compositions on them, and can pursue their areas of special interest in a research paper.

courses.description: Oklahoma!, Carousel, and South Pacific in their political, social, and cultural contexts.

courses.description: Music and spectacle in the late medieval, Renaissance, and baroque courts of Europe.

courses.description: Textual and musical analysis of Verdi's operas (libretto and score) in their sociohistorical contexts.

courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Music in Motion: American Popular Music and Dance
courses.description: The relationship and interplay between musical genres and social dance in different communities and eras.

courses.subject: MUSC

courses.description: The relationship between music and the visual arts in the modernist and postmodernist periods viewed in their historical contexts.

courses.subject: MUSC

courses.description: Music in, and musical settings of, American literature of the Romantic, modern, and postmodern periods.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Reverberations
courses.description: Musical crossovers in world musics and societies.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Vienna: City of Dreams
courses.description: Vienna in the early 1900s as a locus for modernism. Honors version available.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Music on Stage and Screen
courses.description: Offers tools and techniques for understanding multimedia, staged musical works like opera, musical theater, and film. The goal of the seminar is to develop students' analytical skills in verbal and nonverbal media and to encourage their visualization of the potential and implications of artistic forms and structures. Honors version available.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: What is a Work of Art? Listening to Music
courses.description: Musical aesthetics, musical works, and the nature of musical art.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Music and Culture: Understanding the World through Music
courses.description: This seminar focuses on the variety of performances presented by Carolina Performing Arts at Memorial Hall. Through attendance at performances and through research on the performing artists and the works being performed, students explore questions such as, How does music reflect culture? How does the culture shape the art form?

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: A Course in Digital Humanities and Multimedia
courses.description: Bring your own research ideas and learn how to design digital projects for them, including creating visualizations and audio widgets. Learn how to write grant applications for digital humanities, and explore virtual reality projects. Visit the immersion cave at NC State, talk with researchers at Duke's Wired! Lab, and work with programmers at UNC's own Digital Innovation Lab. This class has a particular focus on digital humanities, acoustics, and sound. Honors version available.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Sound Art
courses.description: This course explores the primary concepts, techniques, and artists/works falling under the category of "sound art," a broad, interdisciplinary field that centers sound and listening in contexts outside of traditional musical performance. Examples of sound art include sound installations, environmental listening ("soundwalks"), performance art, conceptual music, novel music technologies, and more. In addition to learning about the history and aesthetics of sound art, students will participate in the creation and public performance of original sound art work.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Foundations in Music
courses.description: An introduction to concepts and methods fundamental to the study, practice, and performance of music. The course provides a foundation for undergraduate students interested in the study of music. Students will gain an appreciation for music's significance across repertories and develop the aptitude to think about music in different ways. Intended for music majors and minors.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Fundamentals of Tonal Music I
courses.description: Notational and theoretical materials of tonal music, with musicianship skills developed. Intended for the nonmajor who wishes to learn basic systems of melody, harmony, rhythm, meter, and form in tonal music and to express musical ideas in five-line staff notation.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Fundamentals of Music II
courses.description: A continuation of MUSC 121 with the addition of basic instrumentation and arranging.

courses.subject: MUSC

courses.description: Basic principles of diction for singers in English/Italian presented through the use of the International Phonetic Alphabet.

courses.description: Basic principles of diction and the International Phonetic Alphabet for singers in French.

courses.subject: MUSC

courses.description: Basic principles of diction and the International Phonetic Alphabet for singers in German.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Improvisation Without Borders
courses.description: This course is an introductory exploration of musical improvisation in non-style specific sound environments. An emphasis will be placed on learning through hands-on performance with one's instrument, voice, and/or computer.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Aural-based Musicianship
courses.description: This course is a study in ear-based performance and analysis, and engages with topics from applied music cognition. This course does not rely on conventional Western ''five-line staff'' musical notation.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Tonal Musicianship Skills I
courses.description: Basic tonal musicianship skills, including music notation, basic composition, score analysis, keyboard, sight singing, and ear training.

courses.title: Tonal Theory I
courses.description: Enrollment subject to a placement test. An introduction to tonal music theory and analysis for students who intend to pursue a music degree. Course covers basic principles of melody, counterpoint, rhythm, and meter. Honors version available.

courses.title: Tonal Theory II
courses.description: A continuation of MUSC 131 , covering more advanced topics of melody, harmony, counterpoint, rhythm, meter, and form. Honors version available.

courses.subject: MUSC

courses.description: This course provides an introduction to music theory--defined as an examination of the underlying patterns deployed by composers, performers, and listeners in creating and comprehending music within a style--for students whose background is primarily aural and/or outside of the notational practices of Western art music or who want to undertake a study of music theory from that perspective.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Survey of Western Music History
courses.description: A chronological survey of the history of Western art music from the Middle Ages to the present. May not count toward the requirements of the music major. May count as credit hours toward graduation, subject to the overall limit on music hours.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Great Musical Works
courses.description: The study of selected works from the Western art music tradition, with an emphasis on critical understanding.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Introduction to Rock Music
courses.description: A survey of rock music history, culture, and musical styles. The course includes extensive listening and an overview of the music's development and evolution.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Introduction to Country Music
courses.description: A survey and investigation of country music from 1920 to the present. This course addresses the music, history, culture, and meaning, across a broad and inclusive of styles, with, with emphasis on critical listening.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Introduction to Jazz
courses.description: A survey of jazz music from its origins to the present. The course builds skills in critical listening and blends discussion of musical materials and historical and cultural contexts.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Introduction to World Musics
courses.description: The study of music in and as culture. Topics may include the performance cultures of Native America, south Asia, Australia, Africa, east Asia, Southeast Asia, Europe, and the Americas.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Introduction to the Music of the Américas
courses.description: An introduction to contemporary Latin(o) American popular music, focusing on how musicians have negotiated an increasingly global popular culture industry.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Introduction to Black Music
courses.description: An introduction to Black musical cultures with a focus on understanding how music is made within social, geographical, and political contexts. The course includes experiential learning, live concert attendance, and conversations with practicing musicians in various musical traditions.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Introduction to Music and Dance
courses.description: Music and dance as human expression, social ritual, and artistic performance across a wide range of repertories, practices, and historical periods.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Introduction to Hip-Hop Music and Culture
courses.description: What are the fundamental understandings and conditions that gave rise to the countercultural phenomenon known as hip-hop? This multimodal, aesthetic movement, fueled by the creativity and ingenuity of Black and Brown youth in the 1970s, challenged consumers of music and popular culture to consider (and take seriously) voices from the margins of society. From the South Bronx to the Dirty South, to West Coast and worldwide, as hip-hop music and culture evolves sonically and stylistically, together we will reflect on hip-hop's origins and maturation, its cultural impact and shortcomings, and its future.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Introduction to the American Stage Musical
courses.description: A topical survey of musical theater repertoire from its early inception in 18th-century Europe to current 21st-century incarnations. Various stylistic approaches, historical periods, and creative contributions to the genre will be explored. Examination of case studies through diverse perspectives of class, gender and race will situate the repertoire in a broad artistic and social context.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Staging Political History: Hamilton and Broadway
courses.description: American stage musicals have engaged with the political history of the United States in substantive and influential ways. This course explores this unique window into history, inviting students to examine primary source materials on which the political foundations of the United States were built. The course then investigates the processes of interpretation, critique, and dissemination of that history as it is transmitted through popular culture. We will consider the role that historians, playwrights, performers, and critics hold in determining how audiences find meaning and make sense of their own political history.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: The Art and Culture of the DJ
courses.description: An exploration of the important, often misunderstood role of the DJ in modern musical life, with particular attention to the ways in which DJing challenges traditional notions of music, musicianship, and musical instruments. Guest lectures, demonstrations, and tutorials by visiting DJs form a significant component of the course.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Beat Making Lab
courses.description: An introductory hands-on study of the composition of electronic instrumental tracks for hip-hop and dance music. Students make beats, learn about the history and culture of the art form, and examine beat making as a case study in entrepreneurship.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Rap Lab
courses.description: A hands-on study of the art of emceeing. Students engage in a rigorous lyricism curriculum, developing the skills to write, recite, and improvise lyrics in live and recorded settings. Students also explore the history of hip-hop culture and analyze the aesthetics of emcees from around the world.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Rock Lab
courses.description: An introduction to issues of performance practice in rock music and related styles and genres including, but not limited to, soul, funk, new wave, and punk. Through intensive coaching and rehearsal students learn performance, transcription, arranging, and improvisation.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Music Production I
courses.description: An in-depth study of vintage and modern music production techniques for jazz, classical, hip-hop, R&B, rock EDM, folk, and other popular forms of music. A focus on digital and analog recording, Pro Tools, and other DAW software basics, microphone techniques, consoles, signal flow, mixing and mastering techniques.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Jazz Improvisation I
courses.description: An introductory course in the development of improvisational skills for the jazz idiom. The primary focus is the introduction of nomenclature, the development of basic jazz vocabulary, and the application of this knowledge using basic jazz tune types.

courses.subject: MUSC
courses.title: Music of South Asia
courses.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the music of South Asia, focusing on India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh. The entire spectrum of musical genres will be covered.

Lesson topics and activities are designed to provide students with practical knowledge and skills pertaining to the craft of composition as well as broad historical and stylistic knowledge of the field beneficial to developing one's artistic voice.

courses.description: Building upon the foundations of MUSC 156 , this course prepares students in professional beat making techniques within various settings of the music industry. The course implements a module-based instruction model, emphasizing student development in creating multiple extended play projects (EPs) with different utilizations (studio, live performance, screen) concluding with the development of a Final Portfolio review, using the computer-based DAW Ableton 11, MIDI controllers, and synthesizers and samplers accessed in the Music Department's Beat Lab.

Because the research and literature in music education and community music is well-developed, we will often borrow strategies and pedagogies that can be applied to nearly any situation to learn and practice how a person can lead others to understand or create music more effectively.
